content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text gives UNDERDETERMINED partly because the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways, which treats a two-sense matter as open.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"\"A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand\": whether 'word-count cuts both ways' is treating a two-sense verse as open (breach), or merely weighing evidence without declaring the verse open (clean).","why":"By grounding UNDERDETERMINED on the word-count cutting both ways, the judge treats the two-sense matter as open instead of letting both senses stand as K-S2 requires."}
